reflection_oracle_classification: I classified the oracle as balanced because the mask [1, 0, 1, 1, 0] contains at least one 1, so the function depends on the parity of selected input bits. The output_offset is 1, which flips every oracle output, but it does not change whether the function is constant or balanced.
reflection_bit_order: The seeded measurement map is reversed, so q[0] is measured into c[4], q[1] into c[3], and so on. The logical result in q[n-1]...q[0] order is 01101, but Qiskit displays counts in c[n-1]...c[0] order, giving 10110 after applying the measurement map.
reflection_hardware_noise: I did not run the optional IBM hardware section. On real hardware I would expect gate errors, readout errors, decoherence, and crosstalk to move some shots away from the ideal bitstring, so the expected result would usually remain prominent but would not necessarily receive all shots.
